newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's route to PM Erbakan's call for elections.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's route to PM Erbakan's call for elections.

text.p: Here is a chronology of the main events leading to the announcement by Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his secularist deputy Tansu Ciller that they would seek new polls.
December 24, 1995 - Erbakan's Welfare Party clinches narrow 21-percent plurality in general polls. Ciller's True Path Party a close third with 20 percent.
June 28, 1996 - Months of bargaining end with Erbakan and Ciller reaching coalition agreement.
July 8 - Islamist-led coalition wins confidence vote.
August 10 - Erbakan arrives in Iran on first foreign visit, calling for close ties with the neighbouring Islamic state.
August 12 - Turkey signs $23 billion deal to import gas through pipeline from Iran despite U.S. protests.
October 6 - Erbakan visits Libya. Opposition outraged by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, who calls for creation of a Kurdish state.
October 16 - Erbakan clears censure vote over Libya visit.
November 3 - Car containing True Path MP, police chief and underworld boss crashes, sparking scandal over state links with criminal gangs.
November 8 - Interior Minister Mehmet Agar of True Path Party resigns over widening car crash scandal.
December 1 - Turkey confirms defence pact with Israel, despite Erbakan's pre-election promises to scrap the deal.

January 10, 1997 - Moslem holy month of Ramadan begins. Welfare promotes Islamist agenda during Ramadan, saying they will lift headscarf ban in public workplaces and build mosques in secularist strongholds.
January 31 - Welfare mayor calls for Islamic law at Islamist protest in Ankara's Sincan district attended by Iranian envoy.
February 1 - Beginning of nightly anti-government protests across Turkey.
February 4 - Tanks parade through Sincan in thinly veiled military warning to Welfare Party.
February 25 - Coalition clears second censure motion.
February 28 - The military-dominated National Security Council demands a government crackdown on religious extremism.
March 4 - MPs drop third censure motion against coalition.
April 4 - Parliament commission investigating state-gangland ties accuses two government MPs of involvement.
April 26 - Two conservative ministers resign in protest against government's refusal to implement anti-Islamist campaign. They begin search for new coalition formula.
April 26 - Army uses monthly National Security Council meeting to renew demands for curb on Islamist activism.
April 29 - Army declares struggle against Islamists a "matter of life and death" for secular republic.
April 30 - Members of an illicit Islamist sect are jailed for three years for anti-secularist actions.
May 11 - Tens of thousands of Islamists rally in Istanbul to protest against planned closing of Koranic schools.
May 17 - Third conservative minister quits government, saying she backs effort to end Islamist rule.
May 19 - MP from Welfare Party resigns and joins main opposition Motherland Party, bringing government's total of deputies -- on paper -- to 280 in 550-seat parliament.
May 20 - Government survives fourth censure motion.
May 21 - Chief prosecutor opens case to close Welfare.
May 22 - Erbakan says he will sue the chief prosecutor.
May 23-24 - Four MPs resign from True Path in two days.
May 30 - The government loses its absolute majority in parliament as a former minister resigns from True Path.
June 1 - Erbakan and Ciller call for early elections.
